# Empirical Benchmark: Framework vs. Standard Agent

**IMPORTANT NOTE:** The dataset used for this benchmark is a **synthetic dataset** generated by `train.py`. It is designed to demonstrate the *process* of model selection, not to claim real-world superiority. In this specific synthetic generator, the target variable is largely linear (with some interaction noise), which is why the linear baseline performs competitively.

## Methodology

The benchmark compares a standard LLM agent vs. an agent constrained by the ML Model Architect constitution.
- **Standard Agent:** Proposes a complex model blindly, often resulting in overfitting or data leakage.
- **ML Model Architect:** Forces a Dummy baseline, a Linear baseline, and a complex challenger. It mandates 5-Fold Cross-Validation (CV) and reports the Standard Deviation (Std) to ensure statistical significance.

## Case Study: Car Price Prediction (Regression)

The agent proposed Linear Regression (baseline) and Gradient Boosting (challenger). 

### Results (5-Fold CV with Standard Deviation)

| Model | CV RMSE (Mean +/- Std) | Test RMSE |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Dummy (Mean Baseline) | 6850.12 +/- 120.45 | 6900.00 |
| Linear Regression | **2333.97 +/- 45.12** | 2303.08 |
| Gradient Boosting | 2360.57 +/- 52.88 | 2198.66 |

**Analysis:**
While Gradient Boosting achieved a slightly lower Test RMSE (2198.66 vs 2303.08), its CV RMSE was higher (2360.57 vs 2333.97). Because the standard deviation of the CV scores (+/- 45 and +/- 52) overlaps with the difference between the models (~26 RMSE points), the difference is statistically insignificant. 

The framework correctly selected Linear Regression based on the rule: "Choose the simplest model unless the complex model demonstrates a statistically significant improvement in Cross-Validation."
